gap_rows.title: rwb-integration ACE plan status: the login, the account resolution, the interface field types, the meaning of live and messageCode, the two settings, the connection-matrix rows and the ownership split are not settled by any one source
gap_rows.source: WP B-P2-01; legacy RWB-E2-002; Ownership Map v1 (GET /cases/{caseId}/plan-status owner P2; interface_config, outbound_item, job_catalog owner P2; lov_value, reference_row, parameter_catalog, parameter_value owner P3; rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row, decision_log_entry owner P7); API Specification v4 /cases/{caseId}/plan-status and the PlanStatus schema; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slides 8, 9, 11, 13, 14, 16, 24, 29, 37, 41, 43, 44 and 45; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1.md slides 11, 12, 14 and 27; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P2 Integration v3.md (scope and REQ-DRI-013); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P2 Integration v3.md T1.1 and T-A.2 API-P2-010; RWB-P3-E2002-APP; RWB-ITG-E2002-ITG
gap_rows.description: One combined gap covers what this slice cannot read from a single source. (1) The rwb-integration login name (DP-02) is given nowhere; the legacy story ran on the shared recovery service identity. (2) The account numbers of the case: the operation is case-scoped and takes the case reference only, while the ACE interface is keyed by account number, so the accounts have to be read first; no source states that the read calls the rwb-case case read, and the work package's contract row names only the parameters, reference-data and rule-catalog contracts. (3) The field types, lengths, required flags, null rules and query shapes of the case read, of the reference-data and parameter answers, of the authorise answer and of the remaining RestructurePlanQuery elements are given nowhere; only the four plan element names are. (4) The meaning of live and messageCode is split across sources: the API Specification carries both fields, the legacy story says live is true when read from ACE now, and neither says who fills the message when the live read fails; the case side needs the flag to choose between the two answers. (5) The two settings rwb.ace.plan.batch-size = 500 and rwb.ace.plan.timeout-ms = 2000 are legacy properties recorded as an assumption under DL11, while DP-06 makes parameters rwb-case data; no source states which owner carries them or how they are read. (6) The connection matrix gives P2 no row to ACE Common and no row to P3, and no row from P3 to P2, although the interface call, the account resolution and the daily call all exist; the omission is a defect of the matrix, not of the design. (7) The ownership split is fixed only by the plan and the Ownership Map: the ACE read and the live answer here, the stored status, the compare, the route state, the rules, the task, the timer, the decision record and the panel in rwb-case, the rights in rwb-access and the package in rwb-decision. (8) The routing of the daily call: the sibling story makes the plan-status step a step of JOB-02 owned by rwb-case, the integration harness lists a plan-status step on rwb-integration, and the job map gives JOB-02 to rwb-case; the sibling and the job map agree and the harness row is the outlier. (9) The stored fallback: the legacy story answers the stored status from the same endpoint, the target splits it into the rwb-case stored answer and this live answer, and the composite route that merges them has no published path or merge order.
gap_rows.evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-002 section 4 step 2 (the case list with account numbers through the P3 CaseQuery), step 3 (statusFor in batches of 500, assumed; DL11), step 8 (the endpoint reads ACE live with a 2-second timeout and falls back to the stored status) and section 12 (PlanStatus: planRef, status, statusDate, live, messageCode; RestructurePlanQuery.statusFor returning planRef, accountNo, status, statusDate); section 13 (properties rwb.ace.plan.batch-size and rwb.ace.plan.timeout-ms, assumed; DL11) and section 17 (no read of another module's tables, ACE data only through the interface). API Specification v4 /cases/{caseId}/plan-status x-module P2, x-capability Case record R, operationId getCasesCaseidPlanStatus, and the PlanStatus schema with planRef, status, statusDate, live and messageCode and no accountNo. TSD P2 v3 T1.1 (v_ace_plan tier 1, API-P2-010) and T-A.2 API-P2-010 (read from v_ace_plan with fallback to plan_status and plan_status_as_of). Arch v5 slide 13 (P2 row: P5 REST and Outside file only; no cell to ACE Common and no cell from P3 to P2), slide 16 (P2 IN GET /interface-runs and POST /interface-runs/{id}/retry, OUT FileDelivered and FileFailed), slide 41 (rwb_integration owns interface config, file runs, outbound items, ACE integration paths), slide 44 (JOB-02 owner rwb-case, mechanism AceDataReady to DailyCaseRun), slide 45 (only rwb-source-data reads the thirty views) and slide 11 (OpenAPI 3.1, one hop, 2 s). RWB-P3-E2002-APP section 4 step 3 (the readPlanStatus activity calls the P2 operation one case per call) and section 12.2. RWB-ITG-E2002-ITG section 12.5 (plan-status step on rwb-integration). No source names the login, the case-read call of this slice, the consumed field types, the messageCode owner, the owner of the two settings or the composite route.
gap_rows.proposed: Settle in the wave 2 contract review: the rwb-integration login with the ACE DB owner; the case read this slice consumes and its contract story; the field sets of the case read, the reference answers, the authorise answer and the remaining interface elements; the owner of live and messageCode with the composite route's merge rule; the owner and read path of the two settings; the P2-to-ACE-Common and P3-to-P2 rows of the connection matrix; and one daily step, in rwb-case. Record the outcome in RWB-P2-E2002-CON, RWB-P2-E2002-OPS, RWB-P3-E2002-APP and the registers; no business value changes in this story.

asm_rows.text: The rwb-integration service runs as one login created with the rwb_integration schema by the platform DB work (DP-02); the story names it "the rwb-integration login" until the name is agreed.
asm_rows.why: No source gives the login name, and every DP-02 row requires one login per service; the legacy story ran on the shared recovery service identity.
asm_rows.read: RWB-P2-E2002-APP sections 3, 10 and 13; DP-02 in Template and Rules section R5.5; Architecture v5 slide 41 (one schema and one login per service).
asm_rows.confirm: ACE DB owner and the platform DB story, before the rwb_integration baseline is created
asm_rows.impact: None on behaviour: the login is named by role in the story and swapped for the agreed name without a content change.

asm_rows.text: The plan is read through the ACE common module's published RestructurePlanQuery.statusFor interface with a 2,000 ms budget per call and batches of 500 account numbers, and not through recovery.v_ace_plan; rwb_integration holds no grant on recovery. The interface is a module interface (INT-34) and not a view, so the direct call of the legacy story stays where the legacy story has it.
asm_rows.why: The Technical Specification reads v_ace_plan with a fallback, while ADR-010, DP-05 and Architecture v5 slide 45 give the thirty views to rwb-source-data alone; the legacy story calls the published interface, and the interface is the only path that keeps a plan engine fact out of the view contract.
asm_rows.read: Legacy RWB-E2-002 section 12 (RestructurePlanQuery.statusFor) and section 4 step 3; TSD P2 Integration v3 T1.1 and T-A.2 API-P2-010; Architecture v5 slides 8, 9, 13, 29, 37, 41 and 45; ADR-010; DP-05 in Template and Rules section R5.5.
asm_rows.confirm: Solution architect and the ACE team at the wave 2 contract review, with the rwb-source-data owner
asm_rows.impact: If the read moves behind rwb-source-data, this story's client and the contract of RWB-P2-E2002-CON change and the batch and budget move to that contract; the answer and the behaviour do not change.

asm_rows.text: The answer of this service is live from ACE on every 200 that read ACE: live is true, the plan fields are the ones ACE returned or absent when it returned no plan, and messageCode is empty. The flag-off answer is 200 with live false and no plan. live false with MSG-P2-008 and the stored date is the rwb-case stored answer on its own base. The composite route takes the live answer when it has one and the stored answer otherwise.
asm_rows.why: The legacy resource carries live and messageCode and answers the stored value from the same endpoint; the split into two providers leaves the flag as the only way for a caller to tell a live value from a stored one, and no source states which provider fills the message.
asm_rows.read: Legacy RWB-E2-002 section 12 (PlanStatus with live false when not live from ACE) and section 5 X2 (the view shows the stored status); API Specification v4 PlanStatus; RWB-P3-E2002-APP AC5 and section 15 (the stored answer carries live false and MSG-P2-008 with its date); DP-19 in Template and Rules section R5.5.
asm_rows.confirm: Case owner (RWB-P3-E2002-APP) and the edge owner (RWB-PLT-N001-CON) at the contract review
asm_rows.impact: If the message moves to this service, the stored date has to be passed to it or read from the case, and the field's rule changes; the flag and the answer shape do not.

asm_rows.text: The RestructurePlanQuery.statusFor answer is taken as a list of plans, one per plan, each carrying planRef, accountNo, status and statusDate for the account numbers asked, and an account with no plan is absent from the list rather than answered as an error or as a null element.
asm_rows.why: The legacy story publishes the four element names and not the null rules, the empty answer or the error of the interface, and the difference between an absent plan and an error decides whether the case side keeps or clears its stored value.
asm_rows.read: Legacy RWB-E2-002 section 12 (List<PlanStatusView> RestructurePlanQuery.statusFor(List<String> accountNos); // planRef, accountNo, status, statusDate) and section 5 X1; RWB-P2-E2002-CON section 12.2.
asm_rows.confirm: The ACE team at the interface review of RWB-P2-E2002-CON
asm_rows.impact: If the interface answers an error for an unknown account, the client maps it to a no-plan answer; the answer shape and the criteria do not change.

asm_rows.text: The account numbers of the case are read through the rwb-case case read by case reference, with the owner and queue, before the ACE call; the authorise answer is taken as a grant of Case record R with the case in or out of scope. The case read and the authorise call are consumed as published contracts and this key holds no copy of a case row or an account row.
asm_rows.why: The operation is case-scoped and takes the case reference only, the ACE interface is keyed by account number, and the rights check needs the owner and queue; no source fixes the read, and the work package's contract row names only three rwb-case contracts.
asm_rows.read: Legacy RWB-E2-002 section 4 step 2 (the cases with their account numbers through the P3 CaseQuery) and section 12 (GET /cases/{caseId}/plan-status, request: path caseId); RWB-P3-E2002-APP section 4 step 3; API Specification v4 x-capability Case record R; DP-11 in Template and Rules section R5.5.
asm_rows.confirm: Case owner (the rwb-case contract baseline) and the access owner at the contract review
asm_rows.impact: If the caller passes the account numbers instead, the client loses one hop and the path keeps a query parameter; the behaviour does not change.

asm_rows.text: The batch size of 500 and the timeout of 2000 ms are read at run time as parameter rows of rwb-case through its parameters contract with the version in force, never as code; a change of the version is picked up without a redeploy, and the deployment carries the same two names as its defaults.
asm_rows.why: The legacy story records both as service properties and marks them assumed under DL11, while DP-06 makes parameters and their versions rwb-case data; a value in code would break the guardrail that no business value sits in code.
asm_rows.read: Legacy RWB-E2-002 section 4 step 3 and section 13 (rwb.ace.plan.batch-size = 500 and rwb.ace.plan.timeout-ms = 2000, assumed; DL11); DP-06 in Template and Rules section R5.5; Ownership Map parameter_catalog and parameter_value owner P3; RWB-P2-E2002-CON section 12.2.
asm_rows.confirm: The parameters owner (RWB-P3-E1042-CON) and the ACE team at the contract review
asm_rows.impact: The two values may change without a release; if they stay deployment values, the read is the values file and no behaviour changes.
